reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that ranking systems must account for both direct performance and indirect strength signals. EWPct is a probabilistic kernel derived from game outcomes, while WPct is a naive aggregate. RPIw introduces transitive strength through opponents’ records. Each primitive fails under asymmetric scheduling or insufficient data. Monte Carlo simulations allow evaluation of these primitives under known team abilities, revealing which methods maintain stable rank ordering. The duality lies in how EWPct and RPIw encode information differently—EWPct encodes outcome probabilities, RPIw encodes relational strength. Failure modes include over-reliance on WPct alone, leading to rank inflation in weak conferences, and misalignment between RPIw and true ability when opponent strength is not well represented.
